endpoints.name: OTA version check
endpoints.returns: Latest OTA metadata for an app_id. Server alive on 2026-07-31 but returns {"status":0,"data":null} for this app — no firmware is served; the app falls back to the four OTA images bundled in its own assets.

cloud.failure_mode: Nothing user-visible stops working. The device is driven entirely over local BLE with no account and no pairing; the cloud only feeds the app's OTA-version check, ads and log/telemetry uploads. OTA images are bundled inside the app itself, so even firmware update survives the backend.

device.name: Magic Display
device.notes:
Bluetooth-controlled LED displays for shoes, bags, hats, crafts. Uses Quintic (NXP QN-series) BLE chipset with QPP (Quintic Private Profile) on service 0xFEE9 (chipset is NOT family-wide Quintic: sibling Shining Glasses hardware is Panchip-based with a 0xFD00 OTA service, so Magic Display variants may likewise differ). All command traffic is AES-128-ECB encrypted by a native library bundled in the app (the key expansion is a JNI native call; the 16-byte key is compiled into the shared object, not present in the app's Java — the recovered key is recorded as static_key on the WRITE1 characteristic below). Commands are fixed 16-byte ASCII-named packets: [length, ASCII_CMD..., params..., zero_pad]. CORRECTION: there is NO connection-time 3-way handshake (the earlier claim was wrong). After connecting, the app simply queries the LED matrix type (STYPE) and parses the response. Bulk image transfer uses DATS (data_transfer_start) framing followed by data frames and DATCP (data_transfer_complete) — that is transfer framing, not an authentication handshake. Supports multiple display sizes: 5x36, 12x48, 14x56, 16x64 (reported via STYPE response). Monochrome 1-bit-per-pixel bitmap encoding (threshold: any RGB channel >= 128 = ON). Device identification by manufacturer-specific adv data: {0x54, 0x52, 0x00, 0x27} ("TR" + 0x0027; BROADCAST_AiTURE_PRODUCT in the app's BLE config). No pairing required. Shares an OEM BLE codebase with Shining Glasses. A secondary Texas Instruments profile (service 0xFFF0 / char 0xFFF1) is also supported for TI-based hardware variants. Also has OTA service at 0xFEE8 (Quintic OTA protocol). FEE9/9600 is the generic Quintic-SDK QPP profile reused by unrelated products (e.g. Zhiyun Crane V2 gimbal), so scanning by service UUID alone false-positives — the manufacturer-data prefix match is the real discriminator. CONFIDENCE: command/UUID mapping HIGH (static analysis of the vendor app); AES key RECOVERED from the app's bundled native AES library — 16 bytes at a fixed offset in the shared object: 34522a5b7a6e492c08090a9d8d2a23f8, identical to the public iDeal LED family key. App-derived, not yet verified against hardware.
Enrich-branch evidence: the app's Java AES wrapper exposes cipher / invCipher / keyExpansion / keyExpansionDefault backed by that native library; its protocol layer encrypts every command before write and decrypts notifications. Bulk pixel/image upload uses DATS on WRITE1, waits for DATSOK, sends data chunks on WRITE2, then sends DATCP and waits for DATCPOK. CORRECTION (2026-08-14, verified against the vendor app — supersedes the 2026-07-31 sibling-derived notes, which were WRONG for this device): bulk image data on WRITE2 (960a) IS AES-128-ECB encrypted. The app splits the payload into 16-byte blocks ([length][up to 15 payload bytes]), encrypts each block in its protocol layer and writes it at a fixed 60 ms pacing (the BLE layer's own encrypt hook is an identity no-op). There is NO per-chunk acknowledgement — the string "REOK" appears nowhere in the app; flow control is timing-only. Only the framing commands are acked (DATS→DATSOK, DATCP→DATCPOK). WRITE3 (960b) is likewise encrypted: live DIY writes go through the same encryption before the write, and the music/rhythm visualizer sends encrypted 16-byte packets ([0x12][14 bytes of packed 4-bit levels]) on the same channel — not the sibling's plain 20-byte pixel writes. Animation upload uses the same DATS/data/DATCP flow as images but with 50 ms pacing. This app has NO multi-frame MANY transaction — a 2026-08-18 re-check finds no MANY/MANCPOK strings and no multi-frame upload class; the MANY <count> <profile> … MANYOK … MANCPOK flow is sibling-only (shining-glasses). STYPE response to a size code: STYPE5X36→536, STYPE5X36N→5360, STYPE12X48→1248, STYPE12X48N→12480, STYPE14X56→1456, STYPE16X64→1664 (N-suffixed variants exist only for 5X36 and 12X48). Additional observed app features include LIGHTON/LIGHTOFF torch control, MODE 7 music/rhythm mode backed by a bundled FFT library, MODE 8/9 connected scroll right/left (daisy-chained displays) with a speed byte, SMVEW DIY sync draw, LEDFIRST/LEDSECOND chained display selection, CALL notification passthrough, SCHD/STSC scheduling (timer response prefix "SBHD"), and ANIM animation selection. Four OTA firmware images are bundled in the app assets: TR1805R03-9_OTA.bin, TR1805R03-10_OTA.bin, TR1806R06-2_OTA.bin, TR1806R06-3_OTA.bin.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central.

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: No provisioning step: the device advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a connection from any central. There is no account, no network credential exchange and no pairing PIN, so a replacement client only has to scan, connect and write.

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect and run the documented initialization sequence, if the spec defines one.

setup.notes: No provisioning. Identify by service UUID and the manufacturer-data prefix rather than by name, since these units advertise without a stable local name.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds this device to a network or an owner, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old client is an Android or iOS phone, remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list as well — a cached bond can keep the phone reconnecting automatically and holding the single available link.

covers: power on/off, brightness, speed, all display modes
DIY sync draw and music/rhythm visualizer
firmware OTA from the app-bundled images
local_access.summary: Full local control over BLE as shipped: connect to the FEE9 QPP service (or FFF0 on TI variants), AES-128-ECB with the static key recorded on WRITE1, no pairing, no account, no cloud dependency at any step.

call_notification.description: Phone-call notification passthrough (CALL status time — Agreement.getCallPhone).

data_transfer_start.description: Start bulk data transfer. hi/lo = big-endian 16-bit data length.

diy_sync_mode.description: DIY sync-draw mode (SMVEW): 1 = enter, 0 = exit, 2 = save-and-exit (Agreement.getEnterDiyCommand/getExitDiyCommand/getExitDiyAndSaveCommand).

multi_frame_animation_start.description: NOT PRESENT in this device's app: a 2026-08-18 re-check finds no MANY/MANCPOK command and no multi-frame upload class — here, animation upload is a plain DATS/DATSOK → data → DATCP/DATCPOK transfer on WRITE2 with 50 ms pacing (vs 60 ms for stills). The multi-frame transaction is sibling-only (shining-glasses DiyMutiAgreement + hardware captures): send "MANY <frameCount> <profile>" (profile 01 = stable/fast, 02/03 slower), wait for MANYOK, upload each frame via the normal DATS/data/DATCP sequence, then send MANCPOK and wait for the MANCPOK reply. Whether Magic Display firmware accepts this flow is unknown — unverified for this device.

query_device_type.description: Query display dimensions. Response on notify: 'STYPE5X36', 'STYPE12X48', 'STYPE16X64', etc. NOTE: the builder for it has no call site in the app — the device pushes its STYPE notification unsolicited after connect, so clients can simply listen.

read_schedule.description: Read back the timer schedule (STSC — Agreement.readTimerLight).

select_animation.description: Select built-in animation frame (ANIM n — Agreement.getImageCommand).

select_display_first.description: Address this unit as the first of a daisy chain (LEDFIRST). Sent on connect based on join order.

select_display_second.description: Address this unit as the second of a daisy chain (LEDSECOND).

set_mode_flash.description: Flash mode; interval in ms, big-endian 16-bit (Agreement.getFlashingScreenCommand).

set_mode_music.description: Music/rhythm mode (MODE 7); level frames go to WRITE3. Backed by libint16fft.so.

set_mode_scroll_left_linked.description: Daisy-chained scroll left across linked displays (MODE 9), with speed byte.

set_mode_scroll_right_linked.description: Daisy-chained scroll right across linked displays (MODE 8), with speed byte.

set_schedule.description: Timer auto on/off schedule (SCHD enable hour minute — Agreement.getTimerLightSwitch). Response to STSC uses prefix 'SBHD'.

torch_on.description: Torch/flashlight on (LIGHTON; distinct from LIGHT brightness — Agreement.getFlashLight).

characteristics.name: Command (WRITE1)
characteristics.notes: AES-128-ECB, fixed static key. Key recovered verbatim from the vendor app's bundled native AES library (16 bytes at a fixed offset in the shared object); identical to the public iDeal LED family key. The key is compiled into the native lib (loaded through a JNI key-expansion call) and is not present in the app's Java at all. App-derived, not yet verified against hardware. Confidence: HIGH structure.

characteristics.name: Bulk Data (WRITE2)
characteristics.notes: Bulk image data channel. Data is sent as AES-128-ECB encrypted 16-byte blocks — [length][up to 15 payload bytes] per block, each block encrypted by the app's protocol layer before the write, with a fixed 60 ms sleep between blocks (animation uploads use 50 ms). There is no per-chunk ack ("REOK" appears nowhere in the app); flow control is timing-only. Only the framing commands on WRITE1 are acked (DATS→DATSOK, DATCP→DATCPOK). The BLE layer's own encrypt hook is an identity no-op; the encryption is applied explicitly by the protocol layer. Verified against the vendor app — supersedes earlier sibling-derived notes claiming unencrypted ~100-byte chunks with REOK flow control.

characteristics.name: Auxiliary (WRITE3)
characteristics.notes: Live DIY pixel writes and music/rhythm visualizer data. Packets are 16-byte and AES-128-ECB encrypted by the app's protocol layer before the write; the visualizer sends [0x12][14 bytes of packed 4-bit levels]. Verified against the vendor app — supersedes earlier sibling-derived notes claiming unencrypted 20-byte 05 RR GG BB II packets.

characteristics.name: TI Command
characteristics.notes: TI-variant command characteristic; same AES-128-ECB native key as WRITE1 (recovered from the bundled native AES library, see there). Both the FFF0 service and the FFF1 characteristic come from the app's BLE manager.

characteristics.name: OTA Write
characteristics.notes: Standard Quintic OTA: host sends meta data (cmd 0x01), then the firmware image in 256-byte packets (cmd 0x02), then data-verify (0x03) and execution-new-code (0x04); the device reports an OtaResult status byte on the notify characteristic (per the app's OTA updater). OTA writes are NOT AES-encrypted — the OTA path writes raw. Four firmware images are bundled in the app assets (TR1805R03-9/-10, TR1806R06-2/-3 OTA bins, ~39 KB each).
